modelEssay.title: How to Balance Job Responsibilities and Personal Interests
modelEssay.content: Balancing job responsibilities and personal interests is a common challenge faced by many professionals. To achieve this equilibrium, one must prioritize effectively and manage time wisely. Firstly, setting clear boundaries between work and personal life is crucial. This can be done by allocating specific hours for work and leisure, ensuring that personal time is respected and not encroached upon by job demands. Secondly, it's important to delegate tasks when possible. By sharing responsibilities with colleagues, one can free up time for pursuing personal interests without compromising job performance. Moreover, engaging in hobbies and interests that can also enhance professional skills is a win-win strategy. For instance, if one is passionate about writing, they might consider writing articles related to their field, which can be both fulfilling and beneficial to their career. In conclusion, balancing job responsibilities and personal interests requires a strategic approach that involves time management, delegation, and finding synergies between work and personal passions.

structureAnalysis.paragraph2: 展开段：具体说明如何通过设定界限、任务分配和结合工作与兴趣来实现平衡
structureAnalysis.paragraph3: 总结段：强调平衡工作和个人兴趣需要策略性的方法，并重申主要观点

transcript.text: My dream is to become an online celebrity of sorts.

transcript.text: So I figured I'd give it a go.

transcript.text: I post a lot on social media anyway, so I've got nothing to lose.
transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: I guess that's true.

transcript.text: Surprisingly, a lot more than I did as a hobby.

transcript.text: It really was a lot to take in.

transcript.text: And I was up well past midnight.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 而且我一直熬到深夜。

transcript.text: I'd say it's paying off though.
transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: I increased the number of people following my accounts by 15% already.
transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: Dr.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 博士

transcript.text: Phillips, you seem to study everything.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 菲利普斯，你似乎研究一切。

transcript.text: I guess that would be fair to say.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我想这么说很公平。

transcript.text: I spend most of my time studying the Big Bang theory and where our universe came from.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我大部分时间都在研究大爆炸理论和我们宇宙的起源。

transcript.text: Can you tell us a little about that?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你能告诉我们一些关于那个的内容吗？

transcript.text: Well, I'm very interested in why the universe exists at all.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 嗯，我非常感兴趣于宇宙为什么存在。

transcript.text: That may sound odd, but the fact is, at the moment of the Big Bang, both matter and antimatter were created.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 这可能听起来奇怪，但事实是，在大爆炸的时刻，物质和反物质都被创造了。

transcript.text: For a short time, and I mean just a fraction of a second, the whole universe was a super hot soup of radiation filled with these particles.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 在短时间内，我指的是仅仅几分之一秒，整个宇宙是一个充满这些粒子的超热辐射汤。

transcript.text: So, what's baffled scientists for so long is, why is there a universe at all?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 所以，困扰科学家这么久的问题是，为什么宇宙会存在？

transcript.text: That's because matter and antimatter are basically opposites of each other.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 那是因为物质和反物质基本上是彼此的对立面。

transcript.text: They are exactly alike, except that they have opposite electrical charges.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 它们完全相同，除了它们带有相反的电荷。

transcript.text: So, when they collide, they destroy each other?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 所以，当它们碰撞时，它们会相互毁灭吗？

transcript.text: Exactly.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 没错。

transcript.text: So, during the first few moments of the Big Bang, the universe was extremely hot and very small.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 所以，在大爆炸的最初几分钟，宇宙极其炎热且非常小。

transcript.text: Matter, and the now more exotic antimatter, would have had little space to avoid each other.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 物质和现在更奇异的反物质，几乎没有空间来避免彼此。

transcript.text: This means that they should have totally wiped each other out, leaving the universe completely barren.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 这意味着它们应该已经完全相互消灭，留下一个完全贫瘠的宇宙。

transcript.text: But a recent study seems to point to the fact that when matter and antimatter were first created, there were slightly more particles of matter, which allowed the universe we all live in to form?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 但最近的一项研究似乎指出，当物质和反物质最初被创造时，物质粒子稍微多一些，这使得我们居住的宇宙得以形成？

transcript.text: Exactly.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 没错。

transcript.text: Because there was slightly more matter, the collisions quickly depleted all the antimatter and left just enough matter to create stars, planets, and eventually us.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 因为物质稍微多一些，碰撞迅速消耗了所有反物质，留下了足够的物质来创造恒星、行星，最终是我们。

transcript.text: Passage 1.
transcript.translation: 篇章1。

transcript.text: In this week's edition of special series on bizarre medical conditions, there's a report of the case of Michelle Myers.
transcript.translation: 在本周关于异常医学状况的特别系列报道中，有一则关于米歇尔·迈尔斯案例的报告。

transcript.text: Myers is an American woman who woke up one day speaking with a British accent, even though she's lived in the United States all her life.
transcript.translation: 迈尔斯是一名美国女性，某天醒来时说着英国口音，尽管她一生都住在美国。

transcript.text: In 2015, Myers went to bed with a terrible headache.
transcript.translation: 2015年，迈尔斯带着严重的头痛上床睡觉。

transcript.text: She woke up sounding like someone from England.
transcript.translation: 她醒来时说话声音像来自英格兰的人。

transcript.text: Her British accent has remained for the past two years.
transcript.translation: 她的英国口音在过去两年中一直保持。

transcript.text: Previously, Myers had woken up speaking in Irish and Australian accents.
transcript.translation: 此前，迈尔斯曾醒来时说着爱尔兰和澳大利亚口音。

transcript.text: However, on both of those occasions, the accents lasted for only a week.
transcript.translation: 然而，在那两次情况中，口音都只持续了一周。

transcript.text: Myers has been diagnosed with Foreign Accent Syndrome.
transcript.translation: 迈尔斯被诊断患有外国口音综合征。

transcript.text: It's a disorder in which a person experiences a sudden change to their speech so that they sound like they are speaking in a foreign accent.
transcript.translation: 这是一种障碍，患者会经历言语的突然变化，使得他们说话听起来像带有外国口音。

transcript.text: The condition is most often caused by a stroke or traumatic brain injury.
transcript.translation: 这种状况最常见的原因是中风或创伤性脑损伤。

transcript.text: Although people with the syndrome have intelligible speech, their manner of speaking is altered in terms of timing and tongue placement, which may distort their pronunciation.
transcript.translation: 尽管患有该综合征的人言语可懂，但他们的说话方式在时机和舌头位置上有所改变，这可能会扭曲他们的发音。

transcript.text: The result is that they may sound foreign when speaking their native language.
transcript.translation: 结果是，他们说母语时可能听起来像外国人。

transcript.text: It's not clear whether Myers has experienced a stroke or other brain damage, but she also has a separate medical condition which can result in loose joints, easily bruised skin, and other problems.
transcript.translation: 尚不清楚迈尔斯是否经历过中风或其他脑损伤，但她还有一种独立的医疗状况，可能导致关节松弛、皮肤易瘀伤和其他问题。

transcript.text: Foreign Accent Syndrome is rare, with only about 60 cases reported within the past century.
transcript.translation: 外国口音综合征很罕见，过去一个世纪中仅报告了大约60例。

transcript.text: However, a different American woman reportedly spoke with a Russian accent in 2010 after she fell down the stairs and hit her head.
transcript.translation: 然而，据报道，另一名美国女性在2010年摔倒撞头后说话带有俄罗斯口音。

transcript.text: Passage 2.

transcript.text: There is something about water that makes it a good metaphor for life.
transcript.translation: 水有某种特质使其成为生命的绝佳隐喻。

transcript.text: That may be one reason why so many people find relief in swimming when life's seas get rough, and it goes some way towards explaining why books about swimming, in which people tackle icy lakes, race in rivers, and overcome oceans, while reflecting on their lives, have recently become so popular.
transcript.translation: 这可能是为什么当生活变得艰难时，那么多人通过游泳找到慰藉的一个原因，并且这也在一定程度上解释了为什么关于游泳的书籍最近变得如此受欢迎，这些书中人们挑战冰冷的湖泊、在河流中竞赛、跨越大洋，同时反思自己的人生。

transcript.text: These books reflect a trend particularly strong in Britain, where swimming in pools is declining, but more and more folks are opting for open water.
transcript.translation: 这些书籍反映了一种在英国尤为强烈的趋势，那里游泳池游泳正在减少，但越来越多的人选择开放水域。

transcript.text: Wild swimming seems to be especially popular among women.
transcript.translation: 野外游泳似乎在女性中特别受欢迎。

transcript.text: Jenny Landreth recently published a guide to the best swimming spots in London.
transcript.translation: Jenny Landreth 最近出版了一本关于伦敦最佳游泳地点的指南。

transcript.text: Her new book, Swell, interweaves her own story with a history of female pioneers who accomplished remarkable feats, and paved the way for future generations.
transcript.translation: 她的新书《Swell》将她自己的故事与女性先驱的历史交织在一起，这些先驱取得了非凡的成就，并为后代铺平了道路。

transcript.text: Notions of modesty restricted women in the Victorian era, but they still swam.
transcript.translation: 端庄的观念限制了维多利亚时代的女性，但她们仍然游泳。

transcript.text: A bathing machine was rolled down to the seashore, so women would not be seen in swimwear.

transcript.text: In 1892, the Gentlewoman's Book of Sport, described a woman swimming in a heavy dress, boots, hat, gloves, and carrying an umbrella.

transcript.text: Today, I'm going to talk about a very special kind of person.
transcript.translation: 今天，我将谈论一种非常特殊的人。

transcript.text: Psychologists call them Masters of Deception.
transcript.translation: 心理学家称他们为欺骗大师。

transcript.text: Those rare individuals with a natural ability to tell with complete confidence when someone is telling a lie.
transcript.translation: 这些罕见的人天生具有完全自信地判断某人是否在说谎的能力。

transcript.text: For decades, researchers and law enforcement agencies have tried to build a machine that will do the same thing.
transcript.translation: 几十年来，研究人员和执法机构一直试图建造能做同样事情的机器。

transcript.text: Now, a company in Massachusetts says that by using magnetic brain scans, they can determine with 97% accuracy whether someone is telling the truth.
transcript.translation: 现在，马萨诸塞州的一家公司声称，通过使用磁性脑扫描，他们能以97%的准确率判断某人是否在说实话。

transcript.text: They hope that the technology will be cleared for use in American courts by early next year.
transcript.translation: 他们希望这项技术能在明年初获准在美国法庭上使用。

transcript.text: But is this really the ultimate tool for you, the lawyers of tomorrow?
transcript.translation: 但这真的是你们——未来的律师——的终极工具吗？

transcript.text: You will not find many brain scientists celebrating this breakthrough.
transcript.translation: 你不会发现许多脑科学家在庆祝这一突破。

transcript.text: The company might be very optimistic, but the ability of their machine to detect deception has not provided credible proof.
transcript.translation: 该公司可能非常乐观，但其机器检测欺骗的能力尚未提供可信的证明。

transcript.text: That's because the technology has not been properly tested in real-world situations.
transcript.translation: 这是因为该技术尚未在真实世界情境中得到适当测试。

transcript.text: In life, there are different kinds of lies and diverse contexts in which they're told.
transcript.translation: 在生活中，有不同类型的谎言和各种讲述谎言的语境。

transcript.text: These differences may elicit different brain responses.
transcript.translation: 这些差异可能引发不同的大脑反应。

transcript.text: Does their hypothesis behind the apply in every case?
transcript.translation: 他们背后的假设是否适用于每种情况？

transcript.text: We don't know the answer because studies done on how reliable this machine is have not yet been duplicated.
transcript.translation: 我们不知道答案，因为关于这台机器可靠性的研究尚未被重复。

transcript.text: Much more research is badly needed.
transcript.translation: 迫切需要更多研究。

transcript.text: Whether the technology is eventually deemed reliable enough for the courts will ultimately be decided by the judges.
transcript.translation: 该技术最终是否被认为足够可靠以用于法庭，将由法官决定。

transcript.text: Let's hope they're wise enough not to be fooled by a machine that claims to determine truthfulness at the flip of a switch.
transcript.translation: 希望他们足够明智，不会被声称只需按一下开关就能判断真实性的机器所愚弄。

transcript.text: They should also be skeptical of the growing tendency to try to reduce all human traits and actions to the level of brain activity.
transcript.translation: 他们还应警惕试图将所有人类特征和行为都归结为大脑活动水平的日益增长的趋势。

transcript.text: Often, they do not map that easily.
transcript.translation: 通常，它们并不那么容易对应。

transcript.text: Moreover, understanding the brain is not the same as understanding the mind.
transcript.translation: 此外，理解大脑不等于理解心灵。

transcript.text: Some researchers have suggested that thoughts cannot properly be seen as purely internal.
transcript.translation: 一些研究者认为，思想不能被恰当地视为纯粹内在的。

transcript.text: Instead, thoughts make sense only in reference to the individual's external world.
transcript.translation: 相反，思想只有在参照个体的外部世界时才有意义。

transcript.text: So while there may be insights to be gained from matching behavior to brain activity, those insights will not necessarily lead to justice in a court of law.
transcript.translation: 因此，尽管从匹配行为与大脑活动中可能获得见解，但这些见解不一定会导致法庭上的正义。

transcript.text: Problems surround the use of machines to spot deception, at least until it has been rigorously tested.
transcript.translation: 使用机器来检测欺骗存在问题，至少在经过严格测试之前是这样。

transcript.text: A high-tech test that can tell when a person is not telling the truth sounds too good to be true.
transcript.translation: 一种能判断一个人是否在说谎的高科技测试听起来好得令人难以置信。

transcript.text: And when something sounds too good to be true, it usually is.
transcript.translation: 当某事听起来好得令人难以置信时，它通常就是如此。

transcript.text: Last week, I attended a research workshop on an island in the South Pacific.
transcript.translation: 上周，我参加了一个在南太平洋一个岛屿上的研究研讨会。

transcript.text: 30 people were present and all except me came from the island called Makalua in the nation of Vanuatu.
transcript.translation: 有30人在场，除了我之外，所有人都来自瓦努阿图一个叫做Makalua的岛屿。

transcript.text: They live in 16 different communities and speak 16 distinct languages.
transcript.translation: 他们居住在16个不同的社区，说16种不同的语言。

transcript.text: In many cases, you could stand at the edge of one village and see the outskirts of the next community yet the residents of each village speak a completely different language.
transcript.translation: 在许多情况下，你可以站在一个村庄的边缘，看到下一个社区的外围，然而每个村庄的居民说一种完全不同的语言。

transcript.text: According to recent work by my colleagues at the Max Planck Institute for the Science of Human History, this island, just 100 kilometers long and 20 kilometers wide, is home to speakers of perhaps 40 different indigenous languages.
transcript.translation: 根据我在马克斯·普朗克人类历史科学研究所的同事们的最新研究，这个岛屿只有100公里长、20公里宽，却是大约40种不同土著语言使用者的家园。

transcript.text: Why so many?
transcript.translation: 为什么这么多？

transcript.text: We could ask this same question of the entire globe.
transcript.translation: 我们可以对整个地球提出同样的问题。

transcript.text: People don't speak one universal language or even a handful.
transcript.translation: 人们不是说一种通用语言，甚至不是几种。

transcript.text: Instead, today our species collectively speaks over 7 ,000 distinct languages.
transcript.translation: 相反，今天我们的物种总共说超过7000种不同的语言。

transcript.text: And these languages are not spread randomly across the planet.
transcript.translation: 而且这些语言并非随机分布在地球上。

transcript.text: For example, far more languages are found in tropical regions than in the mild zones.
transcript.translation: 例如，在热带地区发现的语言远多于温带地区。

transcript.text: The tropical island of New Guinea is home to over 900 languages.
transcript.translation: 热带岛屿新几内亚是超过900种语言的家园。

transcript.text: Russia, 20 times larger, has 105 indigenous languages.
transcript.translation: 俄罗斯，面积大20倍，有105种土著语言。

transcript.text: Even within the tropics, language diversity varies widely.
transcript.translation: 即使在热带地区，语言多样性也差异很大。

transcript.text: For example, the 250,000 people who live on Vanuatu's 80 islands speak 110 different languages.
transcript.translation: 例如，生活在瓦努阿图80个岛屿上的25万人说110种不同的语言。

transcript.text: But in Bangladesh, a population 600 times greater speaks only 41 languages.
transcript.translation: 但在孟加拉国，人口多600倍，却只说41种语言。

transcript.text: How come humans speak so many languages?
transcript.translation: 为什么人类说这么多种语言？

transcript.text: And why are they so unevenly spread across the planet?
transcript.translation: 而且为什么它们在地球上分布如此不均？

transcript.text: As it turns out, we have few clear answers to these fundamental questions about how humanity communicates.
transcript.translation: 事实上，对于人类如何交流的这些基本问题，我们几乎没有明确的答案。

transcript.text: Most people can easily brainstorm possible answers to these intriguing questions.
transcript.translation: 大多数人可以轻松地头脑风暴出这些有趣问题的可能答案。

transcript.text: They hypothesize that language diversity must be about history, cultural differences, mountains or oceans dividing populations.
transcript.translation: 他们假设语言多样性一定与历史、文化差异、山脉或海洋分隔人群有关。

transcript.text: But when our diverse team of researchers from six different disciplines and eight different countries began to review what was known, we were shocked that only a dozen previous studies had been done, including one we ourselves completed on language diversity in the Pacific.
transcript.translation: 但当我们来自六门不同学科和八个不同国家的多样化研究团队开始审视已知情况时，我们震惊地发现只有一打左右的先前研究完成，包括我们自己完成的一个关于太平洋语言多样性的研究。

transcript.text: These prior efforts all examined the degree to which different environmental, social and geographic variables correlated with the number of languages found in a given location.
transcript.translation: 这些先前的努力都检查了不同环境、社会和地理变量与特定地点发现的语言数量的相关程度。

transcript.text: The results varied a lot from one study to another, and no clear patterns emerged.
transcript.translation: 结果在不同研究之间差异很大，没有出现明确的模式。

transcript.text: The studies also ran up against many methodological challenges, the biggest of which centered on the old statistical saying correlation does not equal causation.
transcript.translation: 这些研究也遇到了许多方法论挑战，其中最大的挑战围绕着古老的统计格言：相关性不等于因果关系。

transcript.text: We often hear people say that America is a land of opportunity, a country built on hope to aspire to greatness, on the American dream.
transcript.translation: 我们经常听人说美国是一个充满机会的国家，一个建立在希望和追求伟大之上的国家，基于美国梦。

transcript.text: But is the dream as we once knew it dying?
transcript.translation: 但这个我们曾经熟知的梦想正在消亡吗？

transcript.text: Today's demographics show that the middle class is disappearing and now the richest 1% of the population has amassed more wealth than the bottom 90%.
transcript.translation: 如今的人口统计显示，中产阶级正在消失，现在最富有的1%人口积累的财富超过了底层90%的人口。

transcript.text: Once upon a time, Americans thought that if they worked hard enough, even in the face of adversity, they would be rewarded with success.
transcript.translation: 曾经，美国人认为，只要他们足够努力，即使面对逆境，也会获得成功的回报。

transcript.text: These days though, the divide between rich and poor is greater than it has ever been.
transcript.translation: 然而，如今贫富差距比以往任何时候都更大。

transcript.text: The question is, what is it going to take to change things?
transcript.translation: 问题是，需要什么才能改变现状？

transcript.text: Maybe one day soon, real change will actually be made in our nation and the gap will be eradicated.
transcript.translation: 也许不久的将来，我们的国家会发生真正的改变，差距会被消除。

transcript.text: But what happens in the meantime?
transcript.translation: 但在此期间会发生什么？

transcript.text: Is there something that we can do to help close the gap?
transcript.translation: 我们能做些什么来帮助缩小差距吗？

transcript.text: Is there something that we can do to prove that a little compassion goes a long way?
transcript.translation: 我们能做些什么来证明一点同情心能起很大作用吗？

transcript.text: If we want to fix the problem of the income gap, first we have to understand it.
transcript.translation: 如果我们想解决收入差距问题，首先必须理解它。

transcript.text: It is a grim reality that you can have one person who only makes around $13 ,000 a year, while across town, another is making millions.
transcript.translation: 一个严峻的现实是，一个人可能一年只挣约13,000美元，而在城市的另一边，另一个人却挣着数百万。

transcript.text: For me, it is kind of astonishing.
transcript.translation: 对我来说，这有点令人惊讶。

transcript.text: And if you ask low-income people what's the one thing that would change their life, they'll say a full-time job.
transcript.translation: 如果你问低收入人群，什么能改变他们的生活，他们会说是一份全职工作。

transcript.text: That's all they aspire to.
transcript.translation: 这就是他们所有的渴望。

transcript.text: So why is it so difficult for so many people to find employment?
transcript.translation: 那么，为什么这么多人找工作如此困难？

transcript.text: It partly comes down to profit-driven business models that are built around low-wage work and part-time jobs that don't provide benefits.
transcript.translation: 部分原因是基于低薪工作和不提供福利的兼职工作的利润驱动型商业模式。

transcript.text: Businesses, in order to bolster profits, hire employees as part-time workers only.
transcript.translation: 为了增加利润，企业只雇佣员工作为兼职工作者。

transcript.text: This means they are paid the lowest legal wage and receive no healthcare or other benefits provided to full-time employees.
transcript.translation: 这意味着他们领取最低法定工资，没有获得全职员工所享有的医疗保健或其他福利。

transcript.text: Simultaneously, technological advancement and a global economy has reduced the demand for well-paying blue-collar jobs here in the United States.
transcript.translation: 同时，技术进步和全球经济减少了美国对高薪蓝领工作的需求。

transcript.text: The cumulative effect of these two factors is that many Americans are forced to take two or more part-time jobs, just to make ends meet.
transcript.translation: 这两个因素的累积效应是，许多美国人被迫从事两份或多份兼职工作，仅仅为了维持生计。

transcript.text: What has become obvious to me when it comes to the income gap is that there needs to be an opportunity for the people at the bottom to push them back up and push them into the middle class to give them hope in their lives.
transcript.translation: 对我来说，收入差距问题显而易见的是，需要为底层人群提供机会，将他们推回上去，并推动他们进入中产阶级，给他们生活中的希望。

questionGroups.title: A Pioneering Woman of Science Re-Emerges after 300 Years

material.title: A Pioneering Woman of Science Re-Emerges after 300 Years

paragraphs.text: Maria Sibylla Merian, like many European women of the 17th century, stayed busy managing a household and rearing children. But on top of that, Merian, a German-born woman who lived in the Netherlands, also managed a successful career as an artist, botanist, naturalist and entomologist (昆虫学家).
paragraphs.translation: 玛丽亚·西比拉·梅里安，像17世纪的许多欧洲女性一样，忙于管理家务和抚养孩子。但除此之外，梅里安，一位出生在德国、居住在荷兰的女性，还成功经营了作为艺术家、植物学家、自然学家和昆虫学家（昆虫学家）的职业生涯。

paragraphs.text: "She was a scientist on the level with a lot of people we spend a lot of time talking about," said Kay Etheridge, a biologist at Gettysburg College in Pennsylvania who has been studying the scientific history of Merian's work. "She didn't do as much to change biology as Charles Darwin, but she was significant."
paragraphs.translation: “她是一位与许多我们经常谈论的科学家齐名的科学家，”宾夕法尼亚州盖茨堡学院的生物学家凯·埃瑟里奇说，他一直在研究梅里安工作的科学历史。“她在改变生物学方面不如查尔斯·达尔文那样有影响，但她很重要。”

paragraphs.text: At a time when natural history was a valuable tool for discovery, Merian discovered facts about plants and insects that were not previously known. Her observations helped dismiss the popular belief that insects spontaneously emerged from mud. The knowledge she collected over decades didn't just satisfy those curious about nature, but also provided valuable insights into medicine and science. She was the first to bring together insects and their habitats, including food they ate, into a single ecological composition.
paragraphs.translation: 在自然历史作为发现的重要工具的时代，梅里安发现了以前未知的关于植物和昆虫的事实。她的观察有助于推翻昆虫从泥中自发产生的流行观念。她数十年收集的知识不仅满足了那些对自然好奇的人，还为医学和科学提供了宝贵的见解。她是第一个将昆虫及其栖息地，包括它们所吃的食物，整合到一个单一的生态构成中的人。

paragraphs.text: After years of pleasing a fascinated audience across Europe with books of detailed descriptions and life-size paintings of familiar insects, in 1699 she sailed with her daughter nearly 5,000 miles from the Netherlands to South America to study insects in the jungles of what is now known as Suriname. She was 52 years old. The result was her masterpiece, Metamorphosis Insectorum Surinamensium.
paragraphs.translation: 在多年来用详细描述和实物大小的熟悉昆虫绘画让欧洲观众着迷之后，1699年，她与女儿从荷兰航行近5000英里到南美洲，在现在被称为苏里南的丛林中研究昆虫。她当时52岁。结果是她的杰作《苏里南昆虫变态记》。

paragraphs.text: In her work, she revealed a side of nature so exotic, dramatic and valuable to Europeans of the time that she received much acclaim. But a century later, her findings came under scientific criticism. Shoddy (粗糙的) reproductions of her work along with setbacks to women's roles in 18th- and 19th-century Europe resulted in her efforts being largely forgotten. "It was kind of stunning when she sort of dropped off into oblivion (遗忘)," said Dr. Etheridge. "Victorians started putting women in a box, and they're still trying to crawl out of it."
paragraphs.translation: 在她的作品中，她揭示了自然的一面，如此异国情调、戏剧性和对当时的欧洲人有价值，以至于她获得了许多赞誉。但一个世纪后，她的发现受到了科学的批评。她作品的粗糙复制品以及18和19世纪欧洲女性角色的挫折导致她的努力在很大程度上被遗忘。“当她逐渐被遗忘时，这有点令人震惊，”埃瑟里奇博士说。“维多利亚时代的人开始把女性放进一个盒子里，她们仍在试图爬出来。”

paragraphs.text: Today, the pioneering woman of the sciences has re-emerged. In recent years, feminists, historians and artists have all praised Merian's tenacity (坚韧), talent and inspirational artistic compositions. And now biologists like Dr. Etheridge are digging into the scientific texts that accompanied her art. Three hundred years after her death, Merian will be celebrated at an international symposium in Amsterdam this June.
paragraphs.translation: 今天，这位科学先驱女性重新浮出水面。近年来，女权主义者、历史学家和艺术家都赞扬了梅里安的坚韧、才华和鼓舞人心的艺术构图。现在，像埃瑟里奇博士这样的生物学家正在深入研究伴随她艺术的科学文本。在她去世三百年后，梅里安将在今年六月阿姆斯特丹的一个国际研讨会上受到庆祝。

paragraphs.text: And last month, Metamorphosis Insectorum Surinamensium was republished. It contains 60 plates (插图) and original descriptions, along with stories about Merian's life and updated scientific descriptions. Before writing Metamorphosis, Merian spent decades documenting European plants and insects that she published in a series of books. She began in her 20s, making textless, decorative paintings of flowers with insects. "Then she got really serious," Dr. Etheridge said. Merian started raising insects at home, mostly butterflies and caterpillars. "She would sit up all night until they came out of the pupa (蛹) so she could draw them," she said.
paragraphs.translation: 上个月，《苏里南昆虫变态记》再版。它包含60幅插图和原始描述，以及关于梅里安生平的故事和更新的科学描述。在写《变态记》之前，梅里安花了数十年时间记录欧洲植物和昆虫，她出版了一系列书籍。她20多岁时开始，制作无文字的、装饰性的花卉与昆虫绘画。“然后她变得非常认真，”埃瑟里奇博士说。梅里安开始在家里饲养昆虫，主要是蝴蝶和毛虫。“她会通宵坐着，直到它们从蛹中出来，以便她能画它们，”她说。

paragraphs.text: The results of her decades' worth of careful observations were detailed paintings and descriptions of European insects, followed by unconventional visuals and stories of insects and animals from a land that most at the time could only imagine. It's possible Merian used a magnifying glass to capture the detail of the split tongues of sphinx moths (斯芬克斯飞蛾) depicted in the painting. She wrote that the two tongues combine to form one tube for drinking nectar (花蜜). Some criticized this detail later, saying there was just one tongue, but Merian wasn't wrong. She may have observed the adult moth just as it emerged from its pupa. For a brief moment during that stage of its life cycle, the tongue consists of two tiny half-tubes before merging into one.
paragraphs.translation: 她数十年细心观察的结果是详细的欧洲昆虫绘画和描述，接着是来自当时大多数人只能想象的土地的昆虫和动物的非常规视觉和故事。梅里安可能使用了放大镜来捕捉绘画中描绘的斯芬克斯飞蛾分叉舌头的细节。她写道，两个舌头结合成一个管子来喝花蜜。后来有些人批评这个细节，说只有一个舌头，但梅里安没有错。她可能是在成虫从蛹中出来的那一刻观察到的。在它生命周期的那个短暂阶段，舌头由两个微小的半管组成，然后合并成一个。

paragraphs.text: It may not have been ladylike to depict a giant spider devouring a hummingbird, but when Merian did it at the turn of the 18th century, surprisingly, nobody objected. Dr. Etheridge called it revolutionary. The image, which also contained novel descriptions of ants, fascinated a European audience that was more concerned with the exotic story unfolding before them than the gender of the person who painted it.
paragraphs.translation: 描绘一只巨型蜘蛛吞噬一只蜂鸟可能不淑女，但当梅里安在18世纪之交这样做时，令人惊讶的是，没有人反对。埃瑟里奇博士称之为革命性的。这幅图像还包含了对蚂蚁的新颖描述，迷住了欧洲观众，他们更关心展现在他们面前的异国故事，而不是画家的性别。

paragraphs.text: "All of these things shook up their nice, neat little view," Dr. Etheridge said. But later, people of the Victorian era thought differently. Her work had been reproduced, sometimes incorrectly. A few observations were deemed impossible. "She'd been called a silly woman for saying that a spider could eat a bird," Dr. Etheridge said. But Henry Walter Bates, a friend of Charles Darwin, observed it and put it in book in 1863, proving Merian was correct.
paragraphs.translation: “所有这些事情都动摇了他们美好、整洁的小观点，”埃瑟里奇博士说。但后来，维多利亚时代的人有不同的想法。她的作品被复制，有时不正确。一些观察被认为不可能。“她因为说蜘蛛能吃鸟而被称为愚蠢的女人，”埃瑟里奇博士说。但查尔斯·达尔文的朋友亨利·沃尔特·贝茨观察到了这一点，并于1863年写入书中，证明梅里安是正确的。

paragraphs.text: In the same plate, Merian depicted and described leaf-cutter ants for the first time. "In America there are large ants which can eat whole trees bare as a broom handle in a single night," she wrote in the description. Merian noted how the ants took the leaves below ground to their young. And she wouldn't have known this at the time, but the ants use the leaves to farm fungi (菌类) underground to feed their developing babies.
paragraphs.translation: 在同一幅插图中，梅里安首次描绘和描述了切叶蚁。“在美洲，有大型蚂蚁能在一夜之间吃光整棵树，只剩下扫帚柄，”她在描述中写道。梅里安注意到蚂蚁如何将叶子带到地下给它们的幼崽。她当时不可能知道，但蚂蚁用叶子在地下种植菌类来喂养它们发育中的婴儿。

paragraphs.text: Merian was correct about the giant bird-eating spiders, ants building bridges with their bodies and other details. But in the same drawing, she incorrectly lumped together army and leaf-cutter ants. And instead of showing just the typical pair of eggs in a hummingbird nest, she painted four. She made other mistakes in Metamorphosis Insectorum Surinamensium as well: not every caterpillar and butterfly matched.
paragraphs.translation: 梅里安关于巨型食鸟蜘蛛、蚂蚁用身体搭桥和其他细节是正确的。但在同一幅画中，她错误地将行军蚁和切叶蚁混在一起。而且，她没有展示蜂鸟巢中典型的一对蛋，而是画了四个。她在《苏里南昆虫变态记》中也犯了其他错误：不是每只毛虫和蝴蝶都匹配。

paragraphs.text: Perhaps one explanation for her mistakes is that she cut short her Suriname trip after getting sick, and completed the book at home in Amsterdam. And errors are common among some of history's most-celebrated scientific minds, too. "These errors no more invalidate Ms. Merian's work than do well-known misconceptions published by Charles Darwin or Isaac Newton," Dr. Etheridge wrote in a paper that argued that too many have wrongly focused on the mistakes of her work.
paragraphs.translation: 也许对她错误的一个解释是，她在生病后缩短了苏里南之旅，在阿姆斯特丹的家中完成了这本书。而且，错误在历史上一些最著名的科学头脑中也很常见。“这些错误并不比查尔斯·达尔文或艾萨克·牛顿发表的著名误解更能使梅里安女士的工作失效，”埃瑟里奇博士在一篇论文中写道，他认为太多人错误地关注了她工作中的错误。

paragraphs.text: Merian's paintings inspired artists and ecologists. In an 1801 drawing from his book, General Zoology Amphibia, George Shaw, an English botanist and zoologist, credited Merian for describing a frog in the account of her South American expedition, and named the young tree frog after her in his portrayal of it. It wouldn't be fair to give Merian all the credit. She received assistance naming plants, making sketches and referencing the work of others. Her daughters helped her color her drawings.
paragraphs.translation: 梅里安的绘画启发了艺术家和生态学家。在1801年他的书《两栖动物通史》的一幅画中，英国植物学家和动物学家乔治·肖赞扬梅里安在她南美探险的记述中描述了一种青蛙，并在描绘中以她的名字命名了这种年轻的树蛙。把所有功劳都归于梅里安是不公平的。她在植物命名、制作草图和参考他人作品方面得到了帮助。她的女儿们帮她为画作上色。

paragraphs.text: Merian also made note of the help she received from the natives of Suriname, as well as slaves or servants that assisted her. In some instances she wrote moving passages that included her helpers in descriptions. As she wrote in her description of the peacock flower, "The Indians, who are not treated well by their Dutch masters, use the seeds to abort their children, so that they will not become slaves like themselves. The black slaves from Guinea and Angola have demanded to be well treated, threatening to refuse to have children. In fact, they sometimes take their own lives because they are treated so badly, and because they believe they will be born again, free and living in their own land. They told me this themselves."
paragraphs.translation: 梅里安也记录了从苏里南原住民以及帮助她的奴隶或仆人那里得到的帮助。在某些情况下，她写下了感人的段落，将她的助手包括在描述中。正如她在描述孔雀花时所写：“印第安人，受到荷兰主人的不好对待，用种子来流产他们的孩子，以免他们像自己一样成为奴隶。来自几内亚和安哥拉的黑人奴隶要求得到善待，威胁要拒绝生孩子。事实上，他们有时自杀，因为他们受到如此恶劣的对待，并且因为他们相信他们会重生，自由地生活在自己的土地上。他们亲自告诉了我。”

paragraphs.text: Londa Schiebinger, a professor of the history of science at Stanford University, called this passage rather astonishing. It's particularly striking centuries later when these issues are still prominent in public discussions about social justice and women's rights. "She was ahead of her time," Dr. Etheridge said.
paragraphs.translation: 斯坦福大学科学史教授隆达·席宾格称这段话相当惊人。几个世纪后，当这些问题在关于社会正义和妇女权利的公开讨论中仍然突出时，这尤其引人注目。“她走在了时代前面，”埃瑟里奇博士说。

questions.statementText: Merian was the first scientist to study a type of American ant.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落K。段落K中提到'In the same plate, Merian depicted and described leaf-cutter ants for the first time'（在同一板块中，Merian首次描绘并描述了切叶蚁），这与陈述中的'Merian was the first scientist to study a type of American ant'（Merian是第一个研究一种美国蚂蚁的科学家）相对应。关键词匹配：first scientist对应first time，American ant对应leaf-cutter ants。

questions.statementText: The European audience was more interested in Merian's drawings than her gender.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落I。段落I中提到'The image, which also contained novel descriptions of ants, fascinated a European audience that was more concerned with the exotic story unfolding before them than the gender of the person who painted it'（这幅图像...吸引了一个欧洲观众，他们更关心眼前展开的异国故事，而不是绘画者的性别），这与陈述中的'The European audience was more interested in Merian's drawings than her gender'（欧洲观众对Merian的绘画比她的性别更感兴趣）相对应。关键词匹配：European audience对应European audience，interested in...drawings对应concerned with...story unfolding，her gender对应the gender of the person who painted。

questions.statementText: Merian's masterpiece came under attack a century after its publication.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落E。段落E中提到'But a century later, her findings came under scientific criticism'（但一个世纪后，她的发现受到了科学批评），这与陈述中的'Merian's masterpiece came under attack a century after its publication'（Merian的杰作在其出版一个世纪后遭到攻击）相对应。关键词匹配：came under attack对应came under scientific criticism，a century after its publication对应a century later。

questions.statementText: Merian's mistakes in her drawings may be attributed to her shortened stay in South America.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落M。段落M中提到'Perhaps one explanation for her mistakes is that she cut short her Suriname trip after getting sick, and completed the book at home in Amsterdam'（她错误的原因之一可能是她在苏里南生病后缩短了行程，并在阿姆斯特丹的家中完成了这本书），这与陈述中的'Merian's mistakes in her drawings may be attributed to her shortened stay in South America'（Merian在她的绘画中的错误可能归因于她在南美洲的短暂停留）相对应。关键词匹配：mistakes对应mistakes，shortened stay对应cut short her Suriname trip。

questions.statementText: Merian often sat up the whole night through to observe and draw insects.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落G。段落G中提到'She would sit up all night until they came out of the pupa so she could draw them'（她会整夜坐着直到它们从蛹中出来，这样她就可以画它们），这与陈述中的'Merian often sat up the whole night through to observe and draw insects'（Merian经常整夜坐着观察和画昆虫）相对应。关键词匹配：sat up the whole night through对应sit up all night，observe and draw insects对应came out of the pupa so she could draw them。

questions.statementText: Merian acknowledged the help she got from natives of South America.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落O。段落O中提到'Merian also made note of the help she received from the natives of Suriname, as well as slaves or servants that assisted her'（Merian还提到了她从苏里南的土著，以及帮助她的奴隶或仆人那里得到的帮助），这与陈述中的'Merian acknowledged the help she got from natives of South America'（Merian承认她从南美洲的土著那里得到了帮助）相对应。关键词匹配：acknowledged the help对应made note of the help，natives of South America对应natives of Suriname。

questions.statementText: Merian contributed greatly to people's better understanding of medicine and science.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落C。段落C中提到'The knowledge she collected over decades didn't just satisfy those curious about nature, but also provided valuable insights into medicine and science'（她几十年收集的知识不仅满足了对自然好奇的人，而且还为医学和科学提供了宝贵的见解），这与陈述中的'Merian contributed greatly to people's better understanding of medicine and science'（Merian极大地促进了人们对医学和科学的理解）相对应。关键词匹配：contributed greatly对应provided valuable insights，better understanding对应satisfy those curious about nature。

questions.statementText: Merian occasionally made mistakes in her drawings of insects and birds.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落L。段落L中提到'Merian was correct about the giant bird-eating spiders, ants building bridges with their bodies and other details. But in the same drawing, she incorrectly lumped together army and leaf-cutter ants. And instead of showing just the typical pair of eggs in a hummingbird nest, she painted four. She made other mistakes in Metamorphosis Insectorum Surinamensium as well: not every caterpillar and butterfly matched'（Merian在描述巨型食鸟蜘蛛、用身体建造桥梁的蚂蚁和其他细节方面是正确的。但在同一幅画中，她错误地将兵蚁和切叶蚁混为一谈。而且她没有在蜂鸟巢中只画一对典型的卵，而是画了四个。她在Metamorphosis Insectorum Surinamensium中也犯了其他错误：并非每一个毛虫和蝴蝶都匹配），这与陈述中的'Merian occasionally made mistakes in her drawings of insects and birds'（Merian偶尔在她的昆虫和鸟类绘画中犯错误）相对应。关键词匹配：made mistakes对应made mistakes，drawings of insects and birds对应giant bird-eating spiders, ants...caterpillar and butterfly。

questions.statementText: Now, Merian's role as a female forerunner in sciences has been re-established.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落F。段落F中提到'Today, the pioneering woman of the sciences has re-emerged'（今天，这位科学先锋女性重新出现）以及'Merian will be celebrated at an international symposium in Amsterdam this June'（Merian将在6月的阿姆斯特丹国际研讨会上受到庆祝），这与陈述中的'Now, Merian's role as a female forerunner in sciences has been re-established'（现在，Merian作为科学领域女性先驱的角色已经重新确立）相对应。关键词匹配：re-established对应re-emerged，female forerunner对应pioneering woman。

questions.statementText: Merian made a long voyage to South America to study jungle insects over three centuries ago.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落D。段落D中提到'in 1699 she sailed with her daughter nearly 5,000 miles from the Netherlands to South America to study insects in the jungles of what is now known as Suriname'（在1699年，她和女儿一起航行了近5000英里，从荷兰到南美洲，去研究现在被称为苏里南的丛林中的昆虫），这与陈述中的'Merian made a long voyage to South America to study jungle insects over three centuries ago'（三百多年前，Merian进行了一次长途航行到南美洲研究丛林中的昆虫）相对应。关键词匹配：long voyage对应sailed...nearly 5,000 miles，study jungle insects对应study insects in the jungles，over three centuries ago对应in 1699。

questionGroups.title: Passage One

paragraphs.text: While human achievements in mathematics continue to reach new levels of complexity, many of us who aren't mathematicians at heart (or engineers by trade) may struggle to remember the last time we used calculus (微积分).
paragraphs.translation: 尽管人类在数学领域的成就不断达到新的复杂水平，但我们这些并非天生数学家（或职业工程师）的人，可能很难回忆起上次使用微积分是什么时候。

paragraphs.text: It's a fact not lost on American educators, who amid rising math failure rates are debating how math can better meet the real-life needs of students. Should we change the way math is taught in schools, or eliminate some courses entirely?
paragraphs.translation: 美国教育工作者并未忽视这一事实，在数学不及格率上升的背景下，他们正在辩论数学如何更好地满足学生的实际需求。我们应该改变学校的数学教学方式，还是完全取消一些课程？

paragraphs.text: Andrew Hacker, Queens College political science professor, thinks that advanced algebra and other higher-level math should be cut from curricula in favor of courses with more routine usefulness, like statistics.
paragraphs.translation: 皇后学院政治学教授安德鲁·哈克认为，应该从课程中删减高等代数和其他高等数学，转而开设更具日常实用性的课程，如统计学。

paragraphs.text: "We hear on all sides that we're not teaching enough mathematics, and the Chinese are running rings around us," Hacker says. "I'm suggesting we're teaching too much mathematics to too many people…not everybody has to know calculus. If you're going to become an aeronautical (航空的) engineer, fine. But most of us aren't."
paragraphs.translation: 哈克说：“我们从各方面听到我们教的数学不够，中国人在绕着我们跑。我认为我们给太多人教了太多数学……不是每个人都必须懂微积分。如果你要成为航空工程师，那没问题。但我们大多数人不是。”

paragraphs.text: Instead, Hacker is pushing for more courses like the one he teaches at Queens College: Numeracy 101. There, his students of "citizen statistics" learn to analyze public information like the federal budget and corporate reports. Such courses, Hacker argues, are a remedy for the numerical illiteracy of adults who have completed high-level math like algebra but are unable to calculate the price of, say, a carpet by area.
paragraphs.translation: 相反，哈克在推动更多类似他在皇后学院教授的课程：Numeracy 101。在那里，他的“公民统计学”学生学习分析公共信息，如联邦预算和公司报告。哈克认为，这类课程是治疗那些完成了高等数学（如代数）却无法计算例如地毯按面积价格的成年人的数字文盲的良方。

paragraphs.text: Hacker's argument has met with opposition from other math educators who say what's needed is to help students develop a better relationship with math earlier, rather than teaching them less math altogether.
paragraphs.translation: 哈克的论点遭到了其他数学教育工作者的反对，他们认为需要的是帮助学生更早地与数学建立更好的关系，而不是总体上减少数学教学。

paragraphs.text: Maria Droujkova is a founder of Natural Math, and has taught basic calculus concepts to 5-year-olds. For Droujkova, high-level math is important, and what it could use in American classrooms is an injection of childlike wonder.
paragraphs.translation: 玛丽亚·德鲁约科娃是Natural Math的创始人，并曾向5岁儿童教授基本微积分概念。对德鲁约科娃来说，高等数学很重要，美国课堂上需要注入孩童般的好奇心。

paragraphs.text: "Make mathematics more available," Droujkova says. "Redesign it so it's more accessible to more kinds of people: young children, adults who worry about it, adults who may have had bad experiences."
paragraphs.translation: 德鲁约科娃说：“让数学更容易获得。重新设计它，使其对更多种类的人更容易理解：幼儿、担心数学的成年人、可能有过糟糕经历的成年人。”

paragraphs.text: Pamela Harris, a lecturer at the University of Texas at Austin, has a similar perspective. Harris says that American education is suffering from an epidemic of "fake math"—an emphasis on rote memorization (死记硬背) of formulas and steps, rather than an understanding of how math can influence the ways we see the world.
paragraphs.translation: 德克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校的讲师帕梅拉·哈里斯有类似观点。哈里斯说，美国教育正在遭受“假数学”的流行——强调公式和步骤的死记硬背，而不是理解数学如何影响我们看待世界的方式。

paragraphs.text: Andrew Hacker, for the record, remains skeptical.
paragraphs.translation: 安德鲁·哈克，记录在案，仍然持怀疑态度。

paragraphs.text: "I'm going to leave it to those who are in mathematics to work out the ways to make their subject interesting and exciting so students want to take it," Hacker says. "All that I ask is that alternatives be offered instead of putting all of us on the road to calculus."
paragraphs.translation: 哈克说：“我将留给那些从事数学的人去想办法让他们的学科变得有趣和令人兴奋，这样学生才会想学。我要求的只是提供替代方案，而不是把我们都推上微积分之路。”

questions.questionText: What does the author say about ordinary Americans?

options.label: A
options.text: They struggle to solve math problems.

options.label: B
options.text: They think math is a complex subject.

options.label: C
options.text: They find high-level math of little use.

options.label: D
options.text: They work hard to learn high-level math.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。根据文章第一段中的描述，许多非数学专业或工程领域的美国人可能很难回忆起他们最后一次使用微积分是什么时候，这表明他们认为高级数学对他们的实际生活帮助不大。因此，选项C 'They find high-level math of little use' 是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: 原文并没有提到普通美国人解决数学问题有困难，而是说他们很少使用高级数学。
wrongOptions.B: 原文没有提到普通美国人认为数学复杂，而是讨论了数学教育的问题。
wrongOptions.D: 原文中并没有提到普通美国人努力学习高级数学，而是讨论了是否每个人都需要学习高级数学。

questions.questionText: What is the general complaint about America's math education according to Hacker?

options.label: A
options.text: America is not doing as well as China.

options.label: B
options.text: Math professors are not doing a good job.

options.label: C
options.text: It doesn't help students develop their literacy.

options.label: D
options.text: There has hardly been any innovation for years.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。题目问的是 Hacker 转述的'普遍抱怨'。原文 Hacker 说 'We hear on all sides that we're not teaching enough mathematics, and the Chinese are running rings around us.'（我们从各方面听到我们教的数学不够，中国人在绕着我们跑），这正是他所引述的、社会上普遍存在的抱怨——美国数学教育不如中国。故选项 A 'America is not doing as well as China' 是正确答案。

wrongOptions.B: Hacker并没有批评数学教授的工作，而是批评了数学教育的内容。
wrongOptions.C: '帮助学生发展读写/计算能力'是 Hacker 自己课程的主张，并非他转述的'普遍抱怨'。
wrongOptions.D: Hacker并没有提到美国数学教育缺乏创新，而是认为教授的内容不适合大多数人。

questions.questionText: What does Andrew Hacker's Numeracy 101 aim to do?

options.label: A
options.text: Allow students to learn high-level math step by step.

options.label: B
options.text: Enable students to make practical use of basic math.

options.label: C
options.text: Lay a solid foundation for advanced math studies.

options.label: D
options.text: Help students to develop their analytical abilities.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。根据文章中对Numeracy 101课程的描述，该课程旨在让学生分析公共信息，如联邦预算和公司报告，因此选项B 'Enable students to make practical use of basic math' 是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: Numeracy 101并不是一个高级数学课程，而是一个教授基本数学应用的课程。
wrongOptions.C: 该课程并不是为了高级数学学习打基础，而是为了实际应用。
wrongOptions.D: 虽然该课程可能有助于发展分析能力，但其主要目标是实际应用基本数学。

questions.questionText: What does Maria Droujkova suggest math teachers do in class?

options.label: A
options.text: Make complex concepts easy to understand.

options.label: B
options.text: Start teaching children math at an early age.

options.label: C
options.text: Help children work wonders with calculus.

options.label: D
options.text: Try to arouse students' curiosity in math.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。根据Maria Droujkova的观点，她认为数学教育应该激发儿童的好奇心，所以选项D 'Try to arouse students' curiosity in math' 是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: 虽然理解复杂概念很重要，但这不是Droujkova建议的重点。
wrongOptions.B: Droujkova并没有特别提到从早期开始教数学，而是强调激发好奇心。
wrongOptions.C: Droujkova并没有提到帮助儿童创造奇迹，而是让数学更易于理解和接近。

questions.questionText: What does Pamela Harris think should be the goal of math education?

options.label: A
options.text: To enable learners to understand the world better.

options.label: B
options.text: To help learners to tell fake math from real math.

options.label: C
options.text: To broaden Americans' perspectives on math.

options.label: D
options.text: To exert influence on world development.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。根据Pamela Harris的观点，她认为数学教育的目标应该是帮助学习者更好地理解世界，所以选项A 'To enable learners to understand the world better' 是正确答案。

wrongOptions.B: Harris并没有提到区分真假数学，而是批评了死记硬背的教学方式。
wrongOptions.C: 虽然拓宽美国人对数学的看法可能是一个结果，但不是Harris提到的目标。
wrongOptions.D: Harris并没有提到对世界发展的影响，而是关注于个人如何通过数学看世界。

questionGroups.title: Passage Two

paragraphs.text: For years, the U.S. has experienced a shortage of registered nurses. The Bureau of Labor Statistics projects that while the number of nurses will increase by 19 percent by 2022, demand will grow faster than supply, and that there will be over one million unfilled nursing jobs by then.
paragraphs.translation: 多年来，美国一直面临注册护士短缺的问题。美国劳工统计局预测，尽管到2022年护士数量将增加19%，但需求增长将快于供应，届时将有超过100万个护理职位空缺。

paragraphs.text: So what's the solution? Robots.
paragraphs.translation: 那么解决方案是什么？机器人。

paragraphs.text: Japan is ahead of the curve when it comes to this trend. Toyohashi University of Technology has developed Terapio, a robotic medical cart that can make hospital rounds, deliver medications and other items, and retrieve records. It follows a specific individual, such as a doctor or nurse, who can use it to record and access patient data. This type of robot will likely be one of the first to be implemented in hospitals because it has fairly minimal patient contact.
paragraphs.translation: 日本在这一趋势上处于领先地位。丰桥技术科学大学开发了Terapio，一种机器人医疗推车，可以巡视医院、递送药品和其他物品，并检索记录。它跟随特定个体，如医生或护士，后者可以使用它记录和访问患者数据。这种类型的机器人很可能是首批在医院实施的，因为它与患者的接触相当有限。

paragraphs.text: Robots capable of social engagement help with loneliness as well as cognitive functioning, but the robot itself doesn't have to engage directly—it can serve as an intermediary for human communication. Telepresence robots such as MantaroBot, Vgo, and Giraff can be controlled through a computer, smartphone, or tablet, allowing family members or doctors to remotely monitor patients or Skype them, often via a screen where the robot's 'face' would be. If you can't get to the nursing home to visit grandma, you can use a telepresence robot to hang out with her. A 2016 study found that users had a "consistently positive attitude" about the Giraff robot's ability to enhance communication and decrease feelings of loneliness.
paragraphs.translation: 能够进行社交互动的机器人有助于缓解孤独感并改善认知功能，但机器人本身不必直接参与——它可以作为人类沟通的中介。远程呈现机器人，如MantaroBot、Vgo和Giraff，可以通过计算机、智能手机或平板电脑控制，允许家庭成员或医生远程监控患者或与他们进行Skype通话，通常通过机器人“面部”所在的屏幕。如果你无法去养老院看望祖母，你可以使用远程呈现机器人陪伴她。一项2016年的研究发现，用户对Giraff机器人增强沟通和减少孤独感的能力持“一贯积极的态度”。

paragraphs.text: A robot's appearance affects its ability to successfully interact with humans, which is why the RIKEN-TRI Collaboration Center for Human-Interactive Robot Research decided to develop a robotic nurse that looks like a huge teddy bear. RIBA (Robot for Interactive Body).
paragraphs.translation: 机器人的外观影响其与人类成功互动的能力，这就是为什么RIKEN-TRI人机交互机器人合作研究中心决定开发一个看起来像巨大泰迪熊的护理机器人。RIBA（交互式身体机器人）。

paragraphs.text: On the less cute and more scary side there is Actroid F, which is so human-like that some patients may not know the difference. This conversational robot companion has cameras in its eyes, which allow it to track patients and use appropriate facial expressions and body language in its interactions. During a month-long hospital trial, researchers asked 70 patients how they felt being around the robot and "only three or four said they didn't like having it around."
paragraphs.translation: 在不太可爱且更吓人的一端，有Actroid F，它如此逼真以至于一些患者可能无法分辨区别。这个对话式机器人伴侣眼睛里有摄像头，可以跟踪患者并在互动中使用适当的面部表情和肢体语言。在一个月的医院试验中，研究人员询问了70名患者对机器人在场的感觉，“只有三四个说他们不喜欢它在身边。”

paragraphs.text: It's important to note that robotic nurses don't decide courses of treatment or make diagnoses (though robot doctors and surgeons may not be far off). Instead, they perform routine and laborious tasks, freeing nurses up to attend to patients with immediate needs. This is one industry where it seems the integration of robots will lead to collaboration, not replacement.
paragraphs.translation: 重要的是要注意，护理机器人不决定治疗方案或做出诊断（尽管机器人医生和外科医生可能并不遥远）。相反，它们执行常规和繁重的任务，使护士能够专注于有紧急需求的患者。这是一个机器人整合似乎将导致协作而非替代的行业。

questions.questionText: What do we learn about the robot Terapio?

options.label: A

questions.questionText: What are telepresence robots designed to do?

options.label: A
options.text: Directly interact with patients to prevent them from feeling lonely.

options.label: B
options.text: Cater to the needs of patients for recovering their cognitive capacity.

options.label: C
options.text: Closely monitor the patients' movements and conditions around the clock.

options.label: D
options.text: Facilitate communication between patients and doctors or family members.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。根据文章第三段中的信息，'Telepresence robots such as MantaroBot, Vgo, and Giraff can be controlled through a computer, smartphone, or tablet, allowing family members or doctors to remotely monitor patients or Skype them'，说明远程呈现机器人的设计目的是促进病人与医生或家庭成员之间的沟通，因此D选项是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: 'Directly interact with patients to prevent them from feeling lonely'文章中提到机器人可以作为中介帮助人类沟通，而不是直接与病人互动
wrongOptions.B: 'Cater to the needs of patients for recovering their cognitive capacity'文章中没有提到远程呈现机器人帮助病人恢复认知能力
wrongOptions.C: 'Closely monitor the patients' movements and conditions around the clock'文章中没有提到远程呈现机器人全天候密切监控病人的动态和状况

questionGroups.sourceText: 中国越来越重视公共图书馆，并鼓励人们充分加以利用。新近公布的统计数字表明，中国的公共图书馆数量在逐年增长。许多图书馆通过翻新和扩建，为读者创造了更为安静、舒适的环境。大型公共图书馆不仅提供种类繁多的参考资料，而且定期举办讲座、展览等活动。近年来，也出现了许多数字图书馆，从而节省了存放图书所需的空间。一些图书馆还推出了自助服务系统，使读者借书还书更加方便，进一步满足了读者的需求。

answer.modelTranslation: China is placing increasing emphasis on public libraries and encourages people to make full use of them. Recently released statistics indicate that the number of public libraries in China is growing year by year. Many libraries have created a quieter and more comfortable environment for readers through renovations and expansions. Large public libraries not only offer a wide variety of reference materials but also regularly hold lectures, exhibitions, and other activities. In recent years, numerous digital libraries have emerged, saving space required for storing books. Some libraries have also introduced self-service systems, making it more convenient for readers to borrow and return books, further meeting the needs of readers.
